title: What to Do When Someone Dies in China: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in China: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for China: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: Handling a death in mainland China involves coordinated medical certification, Public Security Bureau (PSB) hukou household registration cancellation, funeral arrangements under updated national rules, and notarized estate settlement under the Civil Code [1][2][3]. Because operational steps vary between municipalities, families should verify local branch procedures alongside national statutes [4][7].

steps.title: Medical Death Certificate and updated 2026 national rules
steps.html:
• Obtain the official Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (Medical Death Certificate) from the attending hospital or designated local health institution, or from public security medical examiners if the death occurred outside a hospital or unexpectedly [1]. Keep multiple original sets, as both civil registration cancellation and funeral arrangements depend on this certificate [1][4].
  • Under the five-department circular led by the National Health Commission (NHC) of the PRC (issued 27 February 2026), unified national coding and formatting for death certificates take effect on 1 July 2026, followed by simultaneous paper and electronic medical death certificates carrying equal legal validity from 1 January 2027 [1].
  • For local municipal workflow illustrations covering hospital release and neighborhood liaison, consult municipal public service portals such as Shanghai Municipal People's Government - Civic Death Procedures Portal [4].

steps.title: Funeral arrangements and Decree No. 824 requirements
steps.html:
• Arrange body custody, cremation or permitted burial, and transport permits strictly through authorized funeral service units in compliance with the Revised Regulations on Funeral and Interment Administration (State Council Decree No. 824), effective 30 March 2026 [3].
  • Present the Medical Death Certificate and family identification documents to the local funeral parlor or civil affairs desk before scheduling cremation or ash interment [1][3][4].
  • Confirm with local civil affairs authorities whether specific municipal subsidies, cremation receipts, or green-burial procedures apply before signing service contracts [3][4].

steps.title: Hukou cancellation and Social Insurance Law survivor benefits
steps.html:
• Present the Medical Death Certificate, household hukou booklet, and the deceased person's resident identity card (or passport and local registration record for foreign nationals) at the local Public Security Bureau Paichusuo police station to cancel household registration [1][4]. Health, public security, and civil affairs agencies jointly coordinate death-certificate cancellation records [1].
  • File claims with the local Social Insurance / Human Resources and Social Security bureau under the Social Insurance Law of the PRC [5]. Individual basic pension account balances are inheritable (Article 14), and qualifying bereaved families may claim funeral subsidies and survivor allowance benefits from basic pension insurance (Article 17) or work-related injury insurance where work-related death applies (Article 38(8)) [5].
  • Note Article 49 of the Social Insurance Law and verify exact local benefit calculation schedules and document lists with the municipal social insurance office [5].

steps.title: Civil Code succession, estate notarization, and deed tax exemptions
steps.html:
• Estate distribution in mainland China is governed by the Civil Code of the PRC (effective 1 January 2021), including Article 1122 (scope of inheritable estate), Article 1127 (order of statutory heirs), Articles 1133-1147 (validity of wills, where the latest legally valid will prevails rather than giving automatic priority to older notarized wills), and Article 1158 (legacy-support agreements) [2].
  • Clarify judicial treatment of care and dependency with reference to Supreme People's Court typical heirship cases (18 December 2024), which enforce legacy-support agreements, protect mandatory shares for heirs lacking labor capability and income sources, recognize equitable shares for non-heirs providing significant support, and deprive heirs guilty of abandonment [7].
  • Apply for an Inheritance Right Notarial Certificate through a local Notary Public Office (for immovables, apply to the notary office at the location of the real property under Articles 11 and 25 of the Notarization Law of the PRC) [6]. Municipal foreign-related notary offices such as Guangzhou Bureau of Justice - Foreign-Related Notary Public Services publish guidance on required family relationship and asset proof [8].
  • Confirm property transfer tax treatment with State Taxation Administration of the PRC [9]: China currently does not impose an inheritance tax, and under Article 6(5) of the Deed Tax Law of the PRC, statutory heirs are exempt from deed tax when inheriting ownership of land or housing (check whether non-statutory testamentary transfers trigger standard assessment) [9].

steps.title: Cross-border Apostille verification and foreign asset filings
steps.html:
• Mainland China joined the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention effective 7 November 2023 [10]. Official notarial certificates (inheritance notarization, death notarization, kinship certificates) required abroad now receive an Apostille issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs or authorized provincial Foreign Affairs Offices listed as Competent Authorities, replacing traditional embassy consular legalization for fellow Convention states [10].
  • Foreign banks, probate courts, and beneficiaries can verify Chinese Apostilles online through Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA) - Consular Apostille Verification [11].
  • Notify domestic and overseas banks, insurers, and employers only after obtaining certified Chinese and translated copies matched to receiving-country rules [6][10].
